details: Bitcoin dropped to approximately $59,100 on June 24, 2026, marking its lowest level since late 2024 and a 53% decline from its October 2025 peak of $126,272. This downturn is attributed to an AI stock sell-off, record Bitcoin ETF outflows (around $6.4 billion over the past month), MicroStrategy's reported Bitcoin sale, and delays in the CLARITY Act. The broader crypto market also saw significant declines, with Ethereum slipping towards $1,500. This environment reflects persistent inflation and dimming hopes for Federal Reserve rate cuts.
title: Bitcoin Falls Below $60K Amid Macro, ETF Outflow Pressures

details: The US Core PCE inflation for May 2026 came in at 3.4%, aligning with expectations but slightly up from the previous 3.3%. This continued inflationary pressure strengthens the case for a more aggressive Federal Reserve. CME Group data suggests a near 47.7% probability of the Fed raising its benchmark rate from 3.75% to 4.00% at its September 16 meeting, indicating market anticipation of a more restrictive monetary policy. This macro environment is considered unfavorable for the short-term cryptocurrency market.
title: US Core PCE Inflation Persists, Supports Hawkish Fed Stance

details: Bank of England official Megan Greene commented that tokenized deposits are likely to surpass stablecoins in prominence within five years, potentially becoming the dominant form of digital money ahead of both stablecoins and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) as commercial banks enhance their offerings. This highlights the ongoing evolution and competition among different forms of digital money.
title: BoE Official: Tokenized Deposits May Outpace Stablecoins
